gene_name: Myosin regulatory light chain sqh (isoform X2)
effect_measure_and_value: kME=0.8454 (module membership, Pearson r with M6 eigengene, n=20). M6 partial r(WG|sex)=-0.5898 (n=20, permutation empirical p=0.001).
host_process: Muscle-protein turnover / maintenance. Formal GSEA over the M6 module (Swiss-Prot orthology, clusterProfiler, two independent rankings) identifies cytoskeleton in muscle cells (KEGG map04820, padj=0.0013) and muscle contraction / sarcomere organisation (GO:0006936, padj=1.5e-7) as the module's significant processes. M6 is causally identified (DAG estimate -3.50 WG units per unit eigengene, p=0.008) and survives permutation null testing (empirical p=0.001, the only module to exceed the 99th percentile of 1,000 shuffles).
linked_taxa: None. This study draws no gene-level host-microbe edges (see network_edges.csv): integration is constructed only at the pathway level (predicted_function_overlap) and the phenotype level (phenotype_concordance), so no cross-layer covariance or gene-taxon link is claimed for any hub gene (manuscript section 3.3).
edge_basis: Not applicable at gene level -- no host-gene-to-microbe edge exists in this network by design. The gene's only cross-layer role is indirect, via its module's partial correlation with weight gain, which is itself the shared axis the microbial phenotype-concordance edges attach to (see network_edges.csv and Fig. final_integrated_network).
mechanism_justification: 83.3% identity to Drosophila myosin regulatory light chain (sqh, Swiss-Prot P40423) triangulates with the formal muscle-cytoskeleton/contraction GSEA signal for M6 -- the strongest single confirmation that M6's negative correlation with growth reflects the energetic cost of muscle-protein turnover rather than an artefact of module construction. Top-ranked hub by kME (0.845) and by rank score across the whole candidate set.
